Rangelands in Change
Exploring Earth’s most extensive socio-ecological systems.

What are rangelands?

Rangelands represent the most extensive land cover type on Earth.

Stoddard et al. (1975) define rangelands as ‘those areas of the world which, due to physical limitations such as low and erratic precipitation, rough topography, poor drainage, or cold temperatures are unsuited to cultivation and serve as a source of forage for native and domestic animals as well as a source of wood products, water, and wildlife’.

Globally, rangelands cover approximately 25-54% of the terrestrial surface, depending on the definition used (AlBukhari et al. 2018; Gamoun et al. 2018; Tiscornia et al. 2019; Briske et al. 2020; ILRI 2021).

These rangelands are critical socio-ecological systems due to their economic, environmental, and socio-cultural importance.

Rangelands of Nepal

Nepal’s rangelands span the high-altitude Trans-Himalayan belt down to the mid-hills, covering critical ecological and pastoral gradients. Nationally, they support extensive livestock production and wildlife corridors.

Provincial Dynamics: Karnali Province

Karnali Province, the largest province in Nepal, is home to diverse rangeland ecosystems. These areas are vital for local livelihoods, supporting pastoral communities and serving as habitats for endemic species.

Field Surveyed Rangelands

We conducted field surveys across various rangeland sites in Nepal, focusing on vegetation composition, soil health, and grazing patterns. These surveys provide ground-truth data to validate remote sensing analyses.
